title: Normalized open coefficient restriction
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For every scheme $T$ and open $U$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-open-immersion], the finite constant coefficient sheaves and their completed inverse limit [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients, def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit] have canonical restriction isomorphisms. They fix constant sections and commute with quotient transitions and limit projections. Module restriction [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars] along these isomorphisms is additive and preserves finite limits and colimits. No invertibility of $\ell$ on $T$ is assumed.

source.place: Tags 098F and 09C3; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0946; sites.tex Tags 00Y0 and 03CO; derived.tex Tag 08TC. Extracted from the corresponding steps of lem-sf-clopen-lisse-complete-localization.

proof.text:
composition into an open subscheme is continuous and cocontinuous, so its
precomposition commutes with sheafification. Apply that comparison to each constant
finite quotient ring; the sheafification units give the constant-section normalization.
Naturality in the quotient homomorphisms gives all transition squares. Precomposition
preserves sectionwise limits, so the inverse limit of the finite comparisons gives the
completion comparison and its projection squares. The underlying abelian-sheaf functor
of module restriction is the same precomposition, even after scalar transport. It
preserves kernels and locally surjective maps, hence is additive and exact. This applies
to the completed ring and every finite quotient, including empty opens.
